doc.title: Jay Leonhart interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Poem for the Milt Hinton tribute CD
summary: He contributed a poem-song to the Milt Hinton tribute set and jokes about Hinton being thirty years older than his wife.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Cool. I’m glad you told me that. I’ll really listen for that. I know you had a nice part in the Milt Hinton tribute CD. I saw your name in there with a nice thing to say.
Oh, yeah, yeah. The one he recorded, yeah. That song has not been recorded yet, that tribute that —
No, that’s not what I was talking about, but I know you had a nice sentiment in that double CD they put out that had that nice book in it.

Right. And I put a poem in it, which is actually a song, which had been performed at his 80th birthday. I’m able to keep track of Milt’s birthday perfectly because he is thirty days [years] to the day older than my wife. So when she has a birthday, he has a birthday and he’s thirty years older. Yet somehow she’s fifty years younger. Now that is an interesting bit of mathematics.
I think you should write a song about that too.
He’s thirty years older than she is, but she is fifty years younger than him. She pulls it off every year.
